name: Tolperisone Hydrochloride
sections: White crystalline powder (hydrochloride), very soluble in water.

In use since the 1960s; after a 2012 EMA referral, use in the EU was restricted to adults with post-stroke spasticity because of hypersensitivity reactions. First approval/introduction: Developed in Hungary in the 1960s (Gedeon Richter).

Blocks voltage-gated sodium and calcium channels in the brainstem reticular formation and spinal cord, inhibiting polysynaptic reflexes; relieves muscle spasm and spasticity without significant sedation. Receptor / target profile: Blocks voltage-gated sodium and calcium channels in the brainstem reticular formation and spinal cord, inhibiting polysynaptic reflexes without sedation.
Summary: Well absorbed; Tmax 0.5–1 h (ER prolongs); high first-pass metabolism (CYP2D6, CYP2C19). Half-life ~2.5 h.
Painful muscle spasm associated with musculoskeletal and degenerative spine disorders (as per local approval)
Conventional: 150–450 mg/day in three divided doses
ER 150 mg: once or twice daily; ER 450 mg: once daily after meals
